city.name: Barcelona
city.ticket_note: a T-casual gives 10 rides for about €12.55

scoring: score = sum of POI weights (must-see sights count 2.5x) + 1.5 x distinct 700 m district cells those POIs fall in, so both geographic spread and headline sights can outrank raw count

all_pois.name: Arc de Triomf
all_pois.description: Red-brick arch built as the gateway to the 1888 World Fair — Moorish, not Roman.

all_pois.name: Arenas de Barcelona
all_pois.description: A Moorish-revival bullring turned shopping centre, with a free rooftop walkway.

all_pois.name: Barcelona Cathedral
all_pois.osm_name: Catedral de la Santa Creu i Santa Eulàlia
all_pois.description: The Gothic cathedral of Santa Eulàlia, with 13 white geese in its cloister — one per year of her life.

all_pois.name: Barcelona Zoo
all_pois.description: Inside the Ciutadella park; once home to Snowflake, the only known albino gorilla.

all_pois.name: Barceloneta Beach
all_pois.description: The city beach that did not exist before 1992, when the Olympics opened the seafront.

all_pois.name: Botanical Garden
all_pois.description: Mediterranean-climate plants from five continents, terraced down the Montjuïc slope.

all_pois.name: CCCB
all_pois.osm_name: Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona
all_pois.description: A former workhouse turned exhibition hall, with a mirrored wall reflecting the skyline.

all_pois.name: Camp Nou
all_pois.description: Europe's largest football stadium, rebuilt around the club's museum.

all_pois.name: Casa Amatller
all_pois.description: Puig i Cadafalch's stepped Flemish gable, next door to Casa Batlló in the Block of Discord.

all_pois.name: Casa Batlló
all_pois.description: The dragon-backed house on Passeig de Gràcia — no straight lines, bone-like balconies.

all_pois.name: Casa Milà (La Pedrera)
all_pois.description: Gaudí's wave-fronted apartment block; the roof is a garden of chimney warriors.

all_pois.name: Casa Vicens
all_pois.description: Gaudí's first house — green tiles and Moorish geometry, opened to visitors only in 2017.

all_pois.name: Columbus Monument
all_pois.description: A 60 m column at the foot of the Rambla; the lift to the top is the cheapest view in town.

all_pois.name: El Born CCM
all_pois.description: A market hall built over the streets flattened in 1714, now excavated beneath your feet.

all_pois.name: Fundació Joan Miró
all_pois.description: Miró's own foundation in a white Sert building full of Mediterranean light.

all_pois.name: La Boqueria
all_pois.osm_name: Mercat de Sant Josep - La Boqueria
all_pois.description: The Rambla's cathedral of food, under a wrought-iron roof of 1914.

all_pois.name: La Rambla
all_pois.description: The 1.2 km promenade down a filled-in stream bed, from Catalunya to the sea.

all_pois.name: MACBA
all_pois.description: Richard Meier's white box of contemporary art, its plaza colonised by skateboarders.

all_pois.name: MNAC
all_pois.description: Romanesque frescoes rescued from Pyrenean churches, in a palace above the Magic Fountain.

all_pois.name: Magic Fountain
all_pois.description: The 1929 fountain that still does its light-and-water show below the MNAC steps.

all_pois.name: Maritime Museum
all_pois.description: The medieval royal shipyards, where galleys were built indoors under stone arches.

all_pois.name: Mercat de Sant Antoni
all_pois.description: A cast-iron market on a Greek-cross plan, reopened in 2018 over Roman road remains.

all_pois.name: Mies van der Rohe Pavilion
all_pois.description: The Barcelona Pavilion — travertine, onyx and a chair that defined a century.

all_pois.name: Montjuïc Castle
all_pois.description: The fortress that shelled the city more than it defended it; now the best 360° viewpoint.

all_pois.name: Museu Picasso
all_pois.description: Five medieval palaces holding the painter's youth — the work before he became Picasso.

all_pois.name: Olympic Stadium
all_pois.description: The 1929 stadium reworked for 1992; the Anella Olímpica around it is free to wander.

all_pois.name: Palau Güell
all_pois.description: Gaudí's early mansion off the Rambla, with a parabolic hall and 20 tiled roof chimneys.

all_pois.name: Palau de la Generalitat
all_pois.osm_name: Palau de la Generalitat de Catalunya
all_pois.description: Seat of Catalan government since 1400 — one of the oldest working government buildings anywhere.

all_pois.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
all_pois.description: Domènech i Montaner's concert hall: an inverted stained-glass skylight over the stalls.

all_pois.name: Parc de la Ciutadella
all_pois.description: The city's central park, with a cascade the young Gaudí helped design.

all_pois.name: Park Güell
all_pois.description: Gaudí's failed housing estate turned mosaic terrace, with the whole city laid out below.

all_pois.name: Passeig de Gràcia
all_pois.description: The boulevard where the bourgeoisie competed by architect; Gaudí won twice.

all_pois.name: Plaça Reial
all_pois.description: Palm-shaded arcaded square off the Rambla; the lampposts are an early Gaudí commission.

all_pois.name: Plaça d'Espanya
all_pois.description: The Venetian-towered gateway to Montjuïc, and one of the city's great traffic circles.

all_pois.name: Plaça de Catalunya
all_pois.description: The hinge between the old city and the Eixample grid, and everyone's meeting point.

all_pois.name: Plaça de Sant Jaume
all_pois.description: Where the city hall faces the Catalan government across the old Roman crossroads.

all_pois.name: Poble Espanyol
all_pois.description: An open-air village of replica Spanish architecture, built for the 1929 Expo and never removed.

all_pois.name: Port Vell
all_pois.description: The old harbour, reclaimed from container yards into a marina and boardwalk.

all_pois.name: Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau
all_pois.osm_name: Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau
all_pois.description: A hospital built as a garden village of mosaic pavilions — the largest art nouveau site in Europe.

all_pois.name: Sagrada Família
all_pois.description: Gaudí's unfinished basilica — a forest of stone columns under stained glass, topped out in 2026.

all_pois.name: Santa Maria del Mar
all_pois.osm_name: Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar
all_pois.description: Catalan Gothic at its purest — built in 55 years by the porters of the Born, and it shows.

all_pois.name: Santa Maria del Pi
all_pois.osm_name: Parròquia Basílica de Santa Maria del Pi
all_pois.description: One vast nave and a rose window the size of a room, on a square of the same name.

all_pois.name: Tibidabo — Sagrat Cor
all_pois.description: The church crowning the city's highest hill, beside a working 1901 funfair.

all_pois.name: Torre Bellesguard
all_pois.description: A little-visited Gaudí castle on the slope of Tibidabo, built over a medieval royal ruin.

all_pois.name: Torre Glòries
all_pois.description: Nouvel's iridescent bullet over the Diagonal — a lift to the viewing deck opened in 2022.

unreachable_pois.name: Port Vell
unreachable_pois.description: The old harbour, reclaimed from container yards into a marina and boardwalk.

unreachable_pois.name: Park Güell
unreachable_pois.description: Gaudí's failed housing estate turned mosaic terrace, with the whole city laid out below.
